blocks.text: The census in this chapter corresponds to the census in Numbers 1, framing the book’s transition between two generations. The first counted the generation at Sinai; this second census counts the generation being prepared to receive its inheritance near Moab. This explains why the chapter closes by emphasizing that, apart from Caleb and Joshua, those counted earlier were no longer present.

The relationship between the two census totals and the scale of Israel’s wilderness population has received substantially different literary and historical interpretations. Because those interpretations remain disputed, the figures should be allowed to stand as the chapter presents them without silently imposing a single reconstruction.

This census begins a larger sequence in the final third of Numbers that prepares the new generation for land inheritance. The chapters that follow address inheritance rulings, Joshua’s commission, land boundaries, towns, and safeguards concerning tribal holdings. The census therefore belongs within a broader transition from the wilderness generation to an ordered people ready to receive land.
